verses.text: I hope you will put up with me while I act a little foolish. Please put up with me!
I am jealous for you with a jealousy that comes from God. I promised you to one husband, to Christ. I want to give you to him like a pure young bride.
But I am afraid that your minds may be led away from your simple and pure love for Christ, just as Eve was tricked by the snake's cunning.

If someone comes and preaches a different Jesus from the one we preached, you put up with it easily enough. You do the same if you receive a different spirit from the one you received, or a different good news from the one you accepted.
I do not think I am in any way less than those "super apostles."
I may not be a trained speaker, but I do have knowledge. We have made this very clear to you in every way.
Was it wrong for me to make myself low so that you could be lifted up? I preached God's good news to you without asking for any pay.
I took money from other churches, as if I were robbing them, so that I could serve you.

When I was with you and needed something, I did not make myself a load for anyone. The brothers who came from Macedonia gave me what I needed. I have kept myself from being a load to you in any way, and I will keep on doing so.
As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, no one in all of Achaia will stop me from boasting about this.
Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
And I will keep on doing what I am doing. Then those people who want a chance to boast that they work just like us will have no chance to do it.
Such men are false apostles. They are workers who lie, pretending to be apostles of Christ.
That is not surprising, because even Satan pretends to be an angel of light.
So it is not surprising if his servants pretend to be servants of what is right. In the end they will get what their actions deserve.
I say again, no one should think I am a fool. But if you do, then accept me as a fool, so that I can boast a little too.
When I boast like this, I am not talking as the Lord would. I am talking like a fool.
Many people boast in a worldly way, so I will boast too.
You think you are so wise, yet you gladly put up with fools!
You even put up with anyone who makes you slaves, or takes everything you have, or takes advantage of you, or acts proud, or slaps you in the face.
I am ashamed to say that we were too weak to do that! But if anyone else dares to boast about something, I am talking like a fool now, I dare to boast about it too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they from Israel? So am I. Are they from Abraham's family? So am I.

Are they servants of Christ? I am out of my mind to talk like this, but I am more of one. I have worked much harder. I have been in prison more often. I have been whipped more times than I can count, and I have faced death again and again.
Five times the Jews gave me thirty-nine lashes.
Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was in a shipwreck. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

I have been on many long journeys. I have been in danger from rivers and from robbers. I have been in danger from my own people and from people who are not Jews. I have been in danger in the city, in the desert and at sea, and in danger from false believers.
I have worked hard and long. Often I have gone without sleep. I have been hungry and thirsty, and often gone without food. I have been cold and without enough clothes.
And besides everything else, every day I carry the worry of caring for all the churches.
If anyone is weak, I feel weak too. If anyone is led into sin, I burn inside.
If I must boast, I will boast about the things that show how weak I am.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is to be praised for ever, knows that I am not lying.
In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas had guards watching the city so that he could arrest me.
But I was let down in a basket through a window in the city wall, and I got away from him.
